turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Pavlov's classical conditioning is a great concept to illustrate.  Let's say we're using jellied eels, a traditional British dish. Imagine a student, Alex, who's never tasted jellied eels before. We start by ringing a bell every time Alex is presented with a plate of jellied eels. At first, Alex might find the smell or sight of jellied eels unpleasant or unfamiliar. But with repeated exposure, Alex starts to associate the sound of the bell with the jellied eels. Eventually, Alex begins to salivate at the sound of the bell alone, even if they're not presented with the actual dish. This is Pavlov's classical conditioning in action - a neutral stimulus (the bell) becomes linked to an unconditioned stimulus (the jellied eels).
